name: Respiratory variants & flu
summary: Early H1N1 flu season in the US; England's GP flu positivity rising
state: UKHSA's 29 Oct report showed flu GP swab positivity in England rising to 11.0%, with ICU admissions edging up, though overall activity was low and COVID falling (UKHSA). In the US, mid-October flu hospitalisations were the highest for that week since 2010–11, driven by a drifted H1N1 strain. UKHSA's next report is due on 5 Nov.
for_you: Eligible people can book flu and COVID vaccines through the NHS. Follow UKHSA advice on staying home when unwell.
rubric_hit: Hemisphere flu season unusually early = Watch

sources.title: UKHSA — National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report, 29 Oct

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
